changes.after: In considering the extent and timing of additional adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate

changes.before: the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point to 3-3/4 to 4 percent.
changes.after: the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point to 3-1/2 to 3‑3/4 percent.

changes.before: and the unemployment rate has edged up but remained low through August; more recent indicators are consistent with these developments.

The Committee judges that reserve balances have declined to ample levels and will initiate purchases of shorter-term Treasury securities as needed to maintain an ample supply of reserves on an ongoing basis.

parsed.rationale: Although the Committee cut again, adding "extent and timing" to the forward guidance signals a likely pause, and a second hawkish dissent (Goolsbee) strengthens that signal. Dropping "remained low" on unemployment and starting reserve-management bill purchases lean dovish but are secondary to the guidance shift.

spans.quote: In considering additional adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate
the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point to 3-3/4 to 4 percent.
and the unemployment rate has edged up but remained low through August; more recent indicators are consistent with these developments.

Voting against this action were Stephen I. Miran, who preferred to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/2 percentage point at this meeting, and Jeffrey R. Schmid, who preferred no change to the target range for the federal funds rate at this meeting.
The Committee decided to conclude the reduction of its aggregate securities holdings on December 1.
In considering the extent and timing of additional adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate
the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point to 3-1/2 to 3‑3/4 percent.
and the unemployment rate has edged up through September. More recent indicators are consistent with these developments.

The Committee judges that reserve balances have declined to ample levels and will initiate purchases of shorter-term Treasury securities as needed to maintain an ample supply of reserves on an ongoing basis.

Voting against this action were Stephen I. Miran, who preferred to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/2 percentage point at this meeting; and Austan D. Goolsbee and Jeffrey R. Schmid, who preferred no change to the target range for the federal funds rate at this meeting.
